raw_case_text:
A 36-year-old male was brought to our emergency department with 5-day history of sharp pain, redness, and photophobia in his right eye (RE). There was no associated eye trauma or contact lens use. Ophthalmic charts were unremarkable until 8 years ago, in which are described four mild episodes of unilateral alternating PUK, more frequent in the winter. Medical background elicited a history of Hepatitis C for at least 10 years and a past of intravenous illicit drug abuse, namely, cocaine and heroin, discontinued when he was arrested and substituted by methadone (45 mg/day). There was no history of CDT.
At the ophthalmological examination in the emergency department he presented a best-corrected visual acuity of 20/30 in the RE and 20/20 in his left eye (LE). Oculomotricity was normal, despite a mild pain in the RE. Biomicroscopy showed in the RE a deep conjunctival hyperemia, a ring shaped peripheral ulcer from 3 to 6 o'clock, with dense white stromal infiltrate and an adjacent area of mild diffuse nonnecrotizing scleritis (Figures 1 and 2). No signs of ocular rosacea or blepharitis were noted. Tyndall and flare were absent. IOP was 17 mmHg bilaterally. LE was unremarkable beside two discrete peripheral ring-like leucomas, sparing the limbus and without evident thinning. Posterior segment was normal in both eyes. After a 5-day course of topical ofloxacin 3 m/mL 2/2 hours + oxytetracycline ointment 5 mg/g 3x day, cyclopentolate 1% 2x day, and artificial tear, the patient was reassessed. Due to lack of clinical improvement systemic corticosteroids (CCT) were also started (oral prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day), with good clinical response. Follow-up evaluations evidenced a BCVA of 20/20, with complete epithelization, and resolution of anterior segment inflammatory signs in approximately two weeks (Figure 3). Systemic workout was negative for CTD (antinuclear antibodies, anti-double strand-DNA, ANCAs, Rheumatoid factor, Liver Kidney Microsomal Type 1 Antibodies, anti-SS-A/Ro, and SS-B/La), with normal complement levels. Additionally, infectious serology for syphilis, HIV, and Hepatitis B virus and Interferon-Gamma Release Assays (IGRA) was also negative. Blood cell count, urinalysis, and hepatic function were normal although with twofold increase in hepatic transaminases. HCV strain was genotype 1a with a RNA viral load over 2,6 million/mL. Cryoglobulin screen revealed mixed type 2 cryoglobulins without rheumatoid factor activity (86 mug/mL), suggesting the diagnosis of PUK in the context of HCV-related cryoglobulinemia. No evidence of active vasculitis was present, namely, constitutional symptoms, purpure, arthralgia, membranous glomerulonephritis, and peripheral neuropathy. Patient was intended to start treatment with pegylated interferon plus ribavirin; however, lack of alcohol abstinence and sporadic illicit drug abuse have deferred treatment. After two years of follow-up, no recurrences of PUK or signs of small-vessel vasculitis were noticed.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 36-year-old male presented with a 5-day history of sharp pain, redness, and photophobia in his right eye.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented to the emergency department with 5 days of acute right ocular pain, redness, and photophobia without trauma or contact lens wear. Topical therapy for 5 days with ofloxacin 3 mg/mL q2h, oxytetracycline 5 mg/g ointment TID, cyclopentolate 1% BID, and artificial tears failed to improve the peripheral corneal ulceration.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection for >=10 years and former intravenous cocaine and heroin abuse, currently on methadone maintenance therapy (45 mg/day). Ophthalmic history was notable for four prior mild episodes of unilateral alternating peripheral ulcerative keratitis (PUK) over the preceding 8 years, occurring predominantly in winter.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for right-eye sharp pain, redness, and photophobia; negative for constitutional symptoms, purpura, arthralgia, hematuria, or peripheral neuropathy. Home medication: oral methadone 45 mg/day.

objective.physical_examination: Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/30 in the right eye (RE) and 20/20 in the left eye (LE), with normal extraocular motility and intraocular pressures of 17 mmHg OU. Slit-lamp examination of the RE showed deep conjunctival hyperemia, a ring-shaped peripheral corneal ulcer from 3 to 6 o'clock with dense white stromal infiltrate, and adjacent mild diffuse non-necrotizing anterior scleritis, with no anterior chamber cells/flare, blepharitis, or ocular rosacea. The LE showed two quiet peripheral ring-like corneal leukomas from prior episodes, and fundoscopy was normal OU.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC, urinalysis, complement levels, and connective tissue autoantibodies (ANA, anti-dsDNA, ANCA, RF, anti-LKM-1, anti-SS-A/Ro, anti-SS-B/La) were normal or negative. Infectious screening for syphilis, HIV, HBV, and tuberculosis (IGRA) was negative. Liver transaminases were elevated twofold, with HCV genotype 1a RNA viral load >2.6 million IU/mL. Serum cryoglobulin screening detected mixed type II cryoglobulins (86 ug/mL) without rheumatoid factor activity.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed recurrent peripheral ulcerative keratitis (PUK) and anterior scleritis secondary to chronic hepatitis C genotype 1a-associated mixed type II cryoglobulinemia (syphilis, HIV, HBV, tuberculosis, and systemic autoimmune vasculitides excluded). Addition of systemic oral prednisolone (1 mg/kg/day) to topical antibiotic/cycloplegic therapy produced complete corneal re-epithelialization, resolution of scleritis, and recovery of 20/20 visual acuity within 2 weeks, with no PUK recurrence over 2 years of follow-up.
